texts.3d7b9b605426: Objective for processing: The ultimate objective is to generate reports for the National Breast Screening Programme and in particular the radiology committee. These reports enable the audit and evaluation of the programme, and in particular identification of issues requiring remedial action. The reports contain no raw data, only aggregate tables and figures. Examples of previous reports and tables are attached. The Programme managers or the committee may suggest we produce further reports. If so, these will similarly only include aggregate tables or graphs. Processing activities: Data will be securely stored, password and firewall protected, in our institute which has the required IG toolkit score. They will only be accessible to myself and Amanda Dibden, a member of my statistical team. The data will be read into the statistical package STATA, which in turn will be used to produce the tables and figures for the reports. Specific outputs expected, include ding target date: The major outputs will be the 30+ tables produced annually for the breast screening programme and the report for the radiology committee (examples of both attached). The tables will be published online, whereas the report is only circulated to the radiology committee. As noted above, either body may suggest we produce further tables or reports, including some for publication in journals. I reiterate that we will adhere strictly to the undertaking above that only aggregate tables and figures will be allowed in the public domain. Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: The major benefit to health is the identification of individual areas of poor performance where remedial action such as enhancement of training is required. The overall results may also suggest generic shifts in policy such as changes to X-ray reader polices or to the recall system, although this would be rarer.
